results.name: network_statistics_average
results.evidence: thiscall(ECX=this): sums a dword field at this+0x18 with stride 0x14 (5 dwords) across this+4 (count) elements into a 64-bit accumulator, then __alldiv's by count -- classic ring-buffer average calculation
results.summary: Computes the average of up to N stored 32-bit samples in a small ring-buffer object, using 64-bit-safe summation and division.

results.name: network_statistics_add_sample
results.evidence: unaff_ESI (this) has count field [1] capped at 0x1e(30) and wrap index [2]; copies a 5-dword sample from EAX into slot at this+3+5*index, then recomputes and caches the average of field[1] of each slot via __alldiv into *this
results.summary: Appends a new 20-byte sample entry into a 30-slot ring buffer object and updates its cached running average.

results.name: autopatch_random_filename_generate
results.evidence: seeds RNG via FUN_006240c2(time^0x33333333) (paired with _rand/__time32 callees), fills a 7-byte buffer with rand()%26+'a', returns pointer to static DAT_006ef914 buffer; sits alongside the autopatch/download subsystem in this region
results.summary: Seeds the RNG from the system clock and writes a random 7-letter lowercase string into a static buffer, likely used as a temporary file name for downloads.

results.name: network_channel_client_disconnect
results.evidence: operates on global handle DAT_0069fdfc via FUN_0061b110/FUN_0061aa50, searches a 16-entry table at DAT_0071c2d4+0x414 (stride 0x60) for a match, then branches between FUN_0061b350/FUN_0061b3f0 depending on whether a match was found
results.summary: Looks up an entry in a small client/machine table and performs one of two cleanup calls on a network channel handle depending on whether the entry was found.

results.name: network_session_set_info
results.evidence: copies 3 caller-supplied strings into global fields DAT_00722798/DAT_007227a0/DAT_007227a8 (consumed later by FUN_00577850's network_channels_open path) and stores param_1 into DAT_007227b8, then registers HS-script global slots 0x33-0x36 with names "dedicated","player_flags","game_flags","game_classic" via FUN_0061bb40
results.summary: Stores host/map/variant name strings and a game-type value into globals used to start a network session, and registers well-known Halo script globals (dedicated, player_flags, game_flags, game_classic).

results.name: game_variant_custom_options_encode
results.evidence: reads ~12 fields (offsets 0x4,0x8,0xc,0x10,0x14,0x18,0x1c,0x20,0x28,0x34,0x38,0x3c) off a struct pointer, including recognizable Halo damage/recharge float constants (0x3f000000=0.5 .. 0x40800000=4.0), and packs them into a bitmask later formatted with sprintf("%d,%d")
results.summary: Packs a custom game variant's numeric/boolean options into a compact bitfield pair for textual ("%d,%d") serialization.

results.name: game_variant_custom_options_decode
results.evidence: sscanf(in_EDX,"%d,%d",&local_8,&local_4) then unpacks local_8's bit ranges back into the same struct offsets (0x1c,0x20,4,0x14,0x10,0xc,0x18,0x28,8,...) that FUN_00576180 packs from -- inverse of that function
results.summary: Parses a "%d,%d" text string and unpacks the bitfields back into a game variant options struct, mirroring game_variant_custom_options_encode.

results.name: server_browser_gametype1_flags_pack
results.evidence: packs 4 boolean fields (ECX[0..3]) into bits 3-6 with a fixed type tag of 1 in bits 0-2, then ORs a 3-bit time-limit-like enumeration (values keyed off ECX+4 == 0,0x708,0xe10,0x1518,9000,18000) into bits 7-9
results.summary: Encodes 4 boolean flags plus a time-limit enumeration into a compact code tagged with type id 1, likely for LAN game-browser advertisement.

results.name: server_browser_gametype1_flags_unpack
results.evidence: decodes bits 3-6 of EAX into 4 booleans at ECX[0..3] and bits 7-9 into a pair of values at ECX[4]/ECX[5], exactly mirroring the bit layout produced by FUN_005767d0
results.summary: Decodes the compact type-1 game flags code produced by server_browser_gametype1_flags_pack back into booleans and a value pair.

results.name: server_browser_gametype2_flags_pack
results.evidence: packs 3 boolean fields from EAX into bits 3-5 with a fixed type tag of 2 in bits 0-2, matching the same tagged-encoding pattern as FUN_005767d0 (tag 1) and FUN_005769c0 (tag 3)
results.summary: Encodes 3 boolean flags into a compact code tagged with type id 2, part of a family of per-game-type option packers.

results.name: server_browser_gametype5_flags_pack
results.evidence: builds a code with fixed base value 5 (tag) and ORs in two clamped 2-bit fields from EDX[0]/EDX[1] at bit positions 3 and 5, part of the same tagged bit-packing family as the other gametypeN_flags_pack functions
results.summary: Encodes two small numeric fields into a compact code tagged with type id 5.

results.name: server_browser_gametype5_flags_unpack
results.evidence: extracts bits 3-4 and 5-6 of ECX, clamping each to the range [0,2], and writes them to EDX[0]/EDX[1] -- the inverse bit layout of FUN_00576960
results.summary: Decodes the compact type-5 code produced by server_browser_gametype5_flags_pack back into two clamped numeric fields.

results.name: server_browser_gametype3_flags_pack
results.evidence: packs 2 booleans and five small integer fields (offsets 4,8,0xc,0x10,0x14 of ECX, widths 2/2/2/2/5 bits) into a code tagged with type id 3 in the low 3 bits, consistent with the sibling gametype1/2/5 packers
results.summary: Encodes two booleans and five small numeric options into a compact code tagged with type id 3.

results.name: server_browser_gametype3_flags_unpack
results.evidence: decodes bits 3/4 into two booleans and then five successive multi-bit fields into ECX+4,+8,+0xc,+0x10,+0x14, exactly the layout produced by FUN_005769c0
results.summary: Decodes the compact type-3 code produced by server_browser_gametype3_flags_pack back into its booleans and numeric fields.

results.name: autopatch_download_complete_callback
results.evidence: searches a 2-entry slot table (DAT_006ef93c, stride 0x14) by id (param_1); on completion (param_2==0) GlobalAlloc's a buffer, copies param_4 bytes from param_3 into it, NUL-terminates, stores pointer/size, and sets slot state to 4 (ready) or 5 (error) via param_2!=0
results.summary: Completion callback for an asynchronous download/read: copies the received data into a heap buffer and marks the matching pool slot ready or errored.

results.name: autopatch_download_worker_thread
results.evidence: thread entry that loops calling Sleep(20 or 1000ms) and FUN_00576bc0 (pool tick) until DAT_007227c8 signals shutdown; created by CreateThread in FUN_00576c30
results.summary: Background worker thread that repeatedly polls the download pool until told to stop.

results.name: autopatch_download_pool_tick
results.evidence: walks the 2-entry slot table, counts active (non -1) entries, frees completed ones (GlobalFree + FUN_0061c030) and resets them to state -1, then calls FUN_0061c020 -- a housekeeping pass over the same table used by autopatch_download_start/get_result
results.summary: Advances/cleans up the small asynchronous download slot table and returns the count of still-active slots.

results.name: autopatch_download_pool_initialize
results.evidence: zero/reset-initializes the 2-entry slot table, creates a named mutex ("mutex_%ld" via __snprintf/CreateMutexA), then CreateThread's FUN_00576b80 (autopatch_download_worker_thread) and sets its priority/resumes it
results.summary: Initializes the asynchronous download slot table and starts its worker thread and synchronization mutex.

results.name: autopatch_download_pool_shutdown
results.evidence: marks remaining table entries in-use, sets shutdown flag DAT_007227c8=1 (the flag autopatch_download_worker_thread polls), waits for the worker thread to exit via GetExitCodeThread, then CloseHandle's the thread and mutex
results.summary: Signals the download pool's worker thread to stop, waits for it to exit, and closes its thread and mutex handles.

results.name: autopatch_download_start
results.evidence: finds a free slot (state==-1) in the 2-entry table, marks it in-progress, then dispatches either FUN_0061bd80(...&LAB_00576a70, FUN_00576ad0,...) (async op with the download-complete callback) when in_EDX==0, or FUN_0061bef0(param_1) otherwise; records the mode flag and resulting handle
results.summary: Starts an asynchronous download (or local file read) into a free pool slot, using autopatch_download_complete_callback for completion, and returns the slot index.

results.name: autopatch_download_get_result
results.evidence: given a slot index in in_ECX (0 or 1), returns success only if the slot's state equals 4 (ready) and its mode flag is 0, then outputs the stored data pointer and size to param_1/param_2
results.summary: Retrieves the completed data pointer and size from a finished download pool slot, if ready.

results.name: autopatch_get_proxy_settings
results.evidence: calls InternetQueryOptionA(INTERNET_OPTION_PROXY) first, then falls back to dynamically loading winhttp.dll and calling WinHttpOpen("HaloPC")/WinHttpGetProxyForUrl("http://www.bungie.net") to resolve an HTTP proxy string, per the referenced strings
results.summary: Determines the HTTP proxy to use for contacting bungie.net, first via WinInet settings and then via WinHTTP's automatic proxy detection.

results.name: autopatch_proxy_initialize
results.evidence: calls FUN_00576f40 (autopatch_get_proxy_settings) then passes the result to thunk_FUN_00622050 and sets a readiness flag DAT_007228d0=1 that FUN_005771e0 waits on before issuing its HTTP request
results.summary: Detects and installs the proxy configuration used by the autopatch HTTP client, then signals it is ready.

results.name: autopatch_version_check_request
results.evidence: fetches the registry Halo version (FUN_005776d0) and DistID (FUN_00577760), busy-waits on the proxy-ready flag DAT_007228d0, then issues a request via FUN_0061c260(0x281b, version, distId, callback,...), clearing DAT_0069fe04 on failure
results.summary: Thread that waits for proxy setup and then sends the current game version and distribution id to check for an update.

results.name: autopatch_check_for_update_start
results.evidence: guards on DAT_0069fe04==-1 (not yet started), references string "currentupdate.cfg", performs some config/text setup via FUN_00555xxx helpers, then CreateThread's FUN_005771e0 (autopatch_version_check_request) and records success/failure in DAT_0069fe04
results.summary: One-time entry point that kicks off the background thread which checks bungie.net for a game update.

results.name: autopatch_launch_updater
results.evidence:
builds a "currentupdate.cfg"-style config via successive __snprintf lines ("gamemode 1
", "url "%s"
", "updateversion "%s"
", "gamecommand "%s %s"
"), fetches the running exe path with GetModuleFileNameA, and (per referenced strings "haloupdate.exe", "%s waitprocessid=%d") is set up to CreateProcessA the external updater
results.summary: Assembles the update configuration file and launches the external haloupdate.exe process, passing the current process id so it can wait for the game to exit.

results.name: registry_get_halo_version
results.evidence: RegOpenKeyExA(HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, "Software\\Microsoft\\Microsoft Games\\Halo"), RegQueryValueExA(..., "Version", ...) into a static buffer, RegCloseKey, returns the buffer
results.summary: Reads the installed game's "Version" value from the Halo registry key and returns it as a string.

results.name: registry_get_dist_id
results.evidence: RegOpenKeyExA on the same Halo registry key, RegQueryValueExA(..., "DistID", ...) reading a 4-byte value, RegCloseKey, returns 0 on any failure
results.summary: Reads the installed game's "DistID" (distribution/channel id) DWORD value from the registry.

results.name: network_session_host_start
results.evidence: calls the real, previously-identified network_channels_open() plus FUN_006175f0/FUN_00616340 with the host/map/variant strings set by network_session_set_info, then FUN_00615530 and FUN_0061b6d0(...,0x319,...) to configure a timeout on the resulting channel object stored in DAT_00722a20
results.summary: Opens the network channel layer and creates a network channel/session object configured with the previously-set host info and a set of message-handler callbacks.

results.name: network_channel_manager_close
results.evidence: if the channel handle DAT_00722a20 is non-zero, marks state DAT_00722a18=2, calls FUN_00577940 (network_channel_manager_update) once more, then FUN_0061b760 and FUN_00616c40(handle) to tear it down and zero the global
results.summary: Tears down the network channel/session object created by network_session_host_start, if one exists.

results.name: network_channel_manager_update
results.evidence: if the channel handle DAT_00722a20 is set and either closing (state==2) or a >999-tick timeout has elapsed (via FUN_00449210), calls FUN_00616c00 to flush/reset it, then always calls FUN_00616cb0 as a per-tick pump
results.summary: Periodic per-frame update for the network channel/session object: flushes it on timeout or close request, then pumps it.

results.name: network_channel_message_dispatch
results.evidence: validates a machine/player index returned by FUN_0045c6f0 against a data-array-style table (DAT_0087a480 with count at +0x20, element size at +0x22, base at +0x34), then special-cases message ids 0x15/0x19 (text/field responses via FUN_00615590/FUN_00616640) or falls through to a vtable handler at *(DAT_006f1d20+0xa0), defaulting to an error string reply
results.summary: Validates an incoming network message's sender against a machine table and dispatches it to a type-specific or generic handler, replying with an error string if invalid.

results.name: autopatch_current_version_string_get
results.evidence: writes the literal ASCII bytes forming the build version string "01.00.10.0621" into the caller-supplied buffer -- matches the target build (retail Halo PC 1.0.10)
results.summary: Writes the hardcoded current game build version string ("01.00.10.0621") into a caller buffer.

results.name: autopatch_version_string_is_outdated
results.evidence: assembles the same hardcoded current-version string as FUN_00578190 ("01.00.10.0621") plus a second fixed baseline string ("01.00.08.0616"), then does dotted-quad-style byte-pair comparisons of the caller-supplied version (in_EDX) against both to decide whether an update is needed
results.summary: Compares a version string against the current build and a minimum baseline build to decide whether the client is out of date.
